extraction_metadata.notes: Extracted from Nature paper 'Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states'. The fiducial marker IS the norm-clamp — it bounds the GPCR's conformational displacement to a specific state, enabling cryoEM observation.

title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
subtitle_or_tagline: Generative protein design + cryoEM fiducial markers for previously intractable GPCR structural states
topic: GPCRs mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes has been challenging. This paper combines generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction to design fiducial markers for cryoEM of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points. The approach enables visualization of previously intractable states. Comparison with co-folding models highlights major gaps in predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations.

components.name: Generative protein design
components.role: Designs fiducial marker proteins that bind specific GPCR conformations

components.name: Fiducial marker
components.role: Bounds the GPCR's conformational displacement (= norm-clamp)

architecture.data_flow: GPCR + ligand → generative design → fiducial marker → cryoEM → certified structure

workflow_steps: Step 1 - GPCR + ligand: receptor samples conformational landscape (inactive/intermediate/active)
Step 2 - Generative design: AI creates fiducial marker for target conformation
Step 3 - Marker binding: marker constrains GPCR to one state (norm-clamp)
Step 4 - CryoEM: marker-constrained GPCR imaged (structure resolvable)
Step 5 - Certification: observed structure within c=2.0 Å of designed state
key_claims: Fiducial markers enable cryoEM of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points
High-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs
Extracellular fiducial marker for beta2-adrenergic receptor enables structural characterization without G-protein
Comparison with co-folding models highlights major gaps in predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations
Generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins
caveats_or_warnings: Major gaps in co-folding models (AlphaFold2 predicts wrong conformational state — the interpretability-vs-certification gap)
Fiducial markers constrain the GPCR to one state — the marker IS the norm-clamp
Without the marker, cryoEM cannot resolve any single state (unbounded landscape)
